insight: One of the most-installed community MCP servers (6k+ GitHub stars, MIT) — gives Claude terminal control and diff-based file edits.
name: Desktop Commander
tagline: Open-source MCP server giving AI clients terminal and file control.
description: Desktop Commander is an open-source Model Context Protocol server that lets MCP clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code run terminal commands, search the file system, and make surgical diff-based edits. It manages long-running processes, reads and writes files (including Excel and PDF), and turns an AI assistant into a hands-on coding and automation agent on your own machine. Free and MIT-licensed, with one of the larger community followings among MCP servers.
edge: A most-installed community MCP server — gives Claude/Cursor terminal control and surgical diff-based file edits.
pros: Terminal + file control for MCP clients
cons: Runs on your local machine only
